blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.recommendation: Flatten the function and name its rules so a reader does not need the plan. (1) Skip empty emails with an early `continue` (`if row.email.is_empty() { continue; }`) instead of wrapping the whole loop body in `if !row.email.is_empty()`. (2) Extract the duplicated seat loop — present in both the `Some` and `None` branches with the same `seat.contains('@')` test — into one helper, e.g. `add_new_seats(db, account_id, seats, existing: &[String]) -> Result<usize, DbError>`, filtering with a named predicate such as `is_seat_email(seat)` and a comment saying why a seat without '@' is silently dropped. (3) The condition `if account.plan != row.plan` is the line a newcomer misreads: nothing says why seats of an existing account are added only when its plan differs from the CSV row (and why the plan itself is then not updated). Name it (`let plan_changed = ...`) and add a comment giving the reason, or a doc line on `import` stating the rule. Also extend the doc comment: "returns how many seats were created" does not say that accounts are created too, nor that rows with an empty email are skipped.
findings.title: `import` nests six levels deep and hides its seat rules in unexplained filters
